items.title: [CRITICAL] Linux kernel (FIPS) vulnerabilities
items.content_text: Several security issues were discovered in the Linux kernel. An attacker could possibly use these to compromise the system. This update corrects flaws in the following subsystems: - x86 architecture; - Hardware monitoring drivers; - OCFS2 file system; - IPv4 networking; - Ethernet bridge; - Netfilter; - XFRM subsystem; (CVE-2025-21656, CVE-2026-63940, CVE-2026-74350, CVE-2026-98432, CVE-2026-99999) Ubuntu. Run apt update and apt upgrade, then reboot if the kernel changed.

items.title: [WATCH] Linux kernel (NVIDIA Tegra) vulnerabilities
items.content_text: It was discovered that some AMD processors did not properly perform Reverse Map Table (RMP) checks when the IOMMU accessed certain host buffers. A local attacker with hypervisor access could possibly use this to trigger an out-of-bounds condition and compromise the integrity of SEV-SNP guest memory. (CVE-2023-20585) Several security issues were discovered in the Linux kernel. An attacker could possibly use these to… Ubuntu 24.04. Run apt update and apt upgrade, then reboot if the kernel changed.

items.title: [WATCH] Debug impls for client session values expose TLS secrets
items.content_text: The Debug implementations of Tls12ClientSessionValue and Tls13ClientSessionValue were derived, and so included the TLS 1.2 master secret or TLS 1.3 resumption PSK in their output. Custom ClientSessionStore implementations that format these values with Debug (for example, when logging) could disclose these secrets to readers of the logs. This conflicts with rustls's [key-material redaction… Used by Agave v4.4.1: rustls 0.23.45. Compiled into the release. Watch for a client release that updates this crate.

items.title: [INFO] Buffered application data sent to outer server after ECH rejection
items.content_text: When a server rejects Encrypted Client Hello (ECH), the client completes the handshake using the outer ClientHello and authenticates the server against the ECH config's public_name. At the end of that handshake, rustls encrypted and queued any application data buffered via ClientConnection::writer() *before* queueing the ech_required alert. The application correctly receives… Used by Agave v4.4.1: rustls 0.23.45. Informational: a dependency of the client, usually no action for operators.

items.title: [INFO] Brotli certificate decompression can allocate up to 1 GiB before authentication
items.content_text: The built-in Brotli certificate decompressor (enabled by the non-default brotli crate feature) bounded the size of the decompressed output, but accepted a peer-selected history window. Brotli's large-window extension was enabled, so a five-byte header could cause an allocation of 1 GiB. A peer can abort a process whose allocator cannot satisfy that request. No trusted certificate is required by the attacker… Used by Agave v4.4.1: rustls 0.23.45. Informational: a dependency of the client, usually no action for operators.

items.title: [INFO] Unauthenticated ServerHello can downgrade later connections to classical key exchange
items.content_text: The client recorded the server-selected key exchange group for each server name when processing the ServerHello, before the server was authenticated. This record is used to predict which key share to send in future ClientHellos to that server name. A network attacker can answer one connection attempt with a ServerHello selecting X25519, and then close the connection. Later ClientHellos for that name carry only an… Used by Agave v4.4.1: rustls 0.23.45. Informational: a dependency of the client, usually no action for operators.

Once a wikilink is created, disable_all_links only disables Link entries, so every enclosing ![[ stays live on the wikilink stack. On ![[![[![[…]]]]]] each of those openers then resolves in turn and rescans… Used by Agave v4.4.1, Jito v4.4.1-jito: pulldown-cmark 0.13.1. Compiled into the release. items.title: [CRITICAL] Linux Kernel Missing Initialization of a Variable Vulnerability
items.content_text: Linux Kernel contains a missing initialization of a variable vulnerability that could allow for unintended modification of page-cache-backed data via failure to preserve the shared-fragment marker during socket buffer coalescing, causing ESP input processing to decrypt shared fragments in place. This vulnerability can be chained with CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 to implant PHP webshells and run commands as… Linux Kernel. Update or mitigate as the vendor advises. CISA lists this flaw as exploited in attacks (deadline 2026-10-31 for US agencies).

A network attacker can answer one connection attempt for a target name with a ServerHello that selects X25519 and close the connection. Later ClientHellos for that name carry one X25519 share while supported_groups still lists X25519MLKEM768 first. If the server… Used by Agave v4.4.1: rustls 0.23.45. A custom session store that logs these values can disclose keys to readers of the logs. Ordinary connection and built-in cache diagnostics remain redacted, and the session-store interface already warns that its values are sensitive. ### Details Derived formatters traverse the session's secret-bearing… Used by Agave v4.4.1: rustls 0.23.45. items.title: [INFO] Rustls: Brotli certificate decompression can allocate an attacker-controlled amount of memory up to 1 GiB before authentication.
items.content_text: Summary The built-in (but disabled by default) Brotli certificate decoder bounds the output buffer but accepts an input-selected history window. A header of five bytes can specify a 1 GiB window allocation. A peer can abort a process whose allocator cannot satisfy that request. A client must enable Brotli and connect to the peer; a server must enable Brotli and request a client certificate. Neither direction… Used by Agave v4.4.1: rustls 0.23.45. Informational: a dependency of the client, usually no action for operators.

When the buffer has zero length, the operating system treats the call as a size query: it writes nothing and returns the size of the attribute value or of the name list. rustix still marked that… Used by Agave v4.4.1, Jito v4.4.1-jito: rustix 1.1.4. These include subtraction, zero counting, division, and Montgomery multiplication. Additionally, UintRef equality could terminate at the first unequal limb, and BoxedMontyForm::invert branched on whether an inverse exists. ## Impact Applications using affected operations… Used by Agave v4.4.1, Jito v4.4.1-jito: crypto-bigint 0.5.5. items.content_text: When Options::ENABLE_WIKILINKS is enabled, a wikilink with a pipe separator and empty display text, such as [[a|]], leaks its child node's sibling chain into the content that follows it. Each such link roughly doubles the number of events the parser yields for the rest of the document, so output grows exponentially with input size: 16 repetitions of [[a|]] (112 bytes) yield 327,676 events, where the fixed… Used by Agave v4.4.1, Jito v4.4.1-jito: pulldown-cmark 0.13.1. items.title: [WATCH] Data from an abandoned stream leaks into the next stream on a reused context
items.content_text: The with_context constructors of the stream encoders and decoders used the borrowed context as it was. When a stream was abandoned on a context, for example an encoder dropped before finish() after an error, whatever it left there was carried into the next stream: the input buffered by the previous encoder (up to 128 KiB, or all of it with zstdmt) became the start of the next frame, and a decoder returned… Used by Agave v4.4.1, Jito v4.4.1-jito: zstd 0.14.0. Compiled into the release. Watch for a client release that updates this crate.

items.title: [WATCH] Use-after-free with CParameter::StableInBuffer
items.content_text: With CParameter::StableInBuffer(true) (experimental feature), the C library keeps a pointer to the input of one streaming call and reads from it in later calls, including flush_stream and end_stream, which take no input. An InBuffer only borrows its slice for one call, so safe code could free it in between, and freed memory was compressed into the frame. The C library behaves this way since zstd 1.5.4… Used by Agave v4.4.1, Jito v4.4.1-jito: zstd-safe 8.0.0. Compiled into the release. Watch for a client release that updates this crate.

items.title: [WATCH] Seekable reads a NULL or out-of-bounds seek table
items.content_text: Seekable did not record whether it was initialized. On a fresh Seekable, or one whose init_buff() failed, decompress, offset_to_frame_index and frame_decompressed_size made the C library read a NULL seek table. After a failed re-initialization, decompress returned data from the refused buffer using the previous seek table. Separately, frame_decompressed_size(num_frames()), on Seekable and… Used by Agave v4.4.1, Jito v4.4.1-jito: zstd-safe 8.0.0. Compiled into the release. Watch for a client release that updates this crate.

items.title: [WATCH] OutBuffer::around_pos exposes uninitialized memory
items.content_text: OutBuffer::around_pos accepted a position past the initialized length of a Vec . The next streaming call then marked everything before the position as initialized, so safe code could read stale heap memory between the vector's previous length and that position. The flaw was corrected by zero-filling that gap. Used by Agave v4.4.1, Jito v4.4.1-jito: zstd-safe 8.0.0. Compiled into the release. Watch for a client release that updates this crate.

items.title: [WATCH] Seekable::decompress sets a Vec length beyond its capacity for offsets past the end
items.content_text: ZSTD_seekable_decompress shortens the requested length to the end of the data without checking that the offset is before it. For an offset past the end, it returns a wrapped-around length without writing anything, and Seekable::decompress passed that length to Vec::set_len. With the seekable feature, whoever supplies the archive, or chooses the offset, can leave the caller's Vec with a length far beyond… Used by Agave v4.4.1, Jito v4.4.1-jito: zstd-safe 8.0.0. Compiled into the release. Watch for a client release that updates this crate.

items.title: [WATCH] Use-after-free through init_using_cdict and init_using_ddict
items.content_text: CCtx::init_using_cdict and DCtx::init_using_ddict (experimental feature, deprecated) took the dictionary as &CDict and &DDict with only 'b: 'a, so the dictionary itself could be dropped while the context still pointed at it. The same mistake in other constructors was fixed earlier ( ). The flaw was corrected by taking &'a CDict and &'a DDict . Used by Agave v4.4.1, Jito v4.4.1-jito: zstd-safe 8.0.0. When a stream was left unfinished on a context, a one-shot call such as decompress_using_dict could leave the context pointing at the dictionary borrowed for that call, and the next streaming call resumed the stream against it after it was freed: decompressed output then contained freed heap… Used by Agave v4.4.1, Jito v4.4.1-jito: zstd-safe 8.0.0. With overflow checks off, as in release builds, that sum wrapped around: sizes totalling 2^64 plus the buffer length passed the check, and the trainer read past the end of the buffer. zstd::dict::from_continuous relies on this check from zstd 0.4.10; older versions of zstd had… Used by Agave v4.4.1, Jito v4.4.1-jito: zstd-safe 8.0.0. items.title: [WATCH] Heap buffer overflow in CCtx::try_clone on a multithreaded context
items.content_text: CCtx::try_clone (experimental feature, deprecated) copies tables sized from the context's applied parameters. Starting a multithreaded frame (zstdmt feature) replaces those parameters with the workers' without resizing the context's own tables, so after an abandoned single-threaded frame, the copy wrote up to 512 KiB past a heap allocation, or read past one. This became reachable with the bundled zstd 1.5.6… Used by Agave v4.4.1, Jito v4.4.1-jito: zstd-safe 8.0.0. Compiled into the release. Watch for a client release that updates this crate.

items.title: [WATCH] Uninitialized memory exposed when streaming decompression of a legacy frame fails
items.content_text: When decompression fails inside a legacy (zstd v0.4 to v0.7) frame, the bundled zstd library reports the output buffer as fully written although nothing was written. DCtx::decompress_stream committed that position even on error, and for a Vec destination this extended the vector's length over uninitialized memory. Legacy support is enabled by default. A 5- or 6-byte corrupt legacy frame is enough: through… Used by Agave v4.4.1, Jito v4.4.1-jito: zstd-safe 8.0.0. Compiled into the release. Watch for a client release that updates this crate.

items.title: [WATCH] Double free in DCtx::try_clone
items.content_text: DCtx::try_clone (experimental feature, deprecated) is a plain copy of the C context. A context owning a dictionary (from load_dictionary, ref_prefix or init_using_dict) or a dictionary table (ref_ddict with RefMultipleDDicts) ended up with both copies freeing it. A context cloned mid-frame resumed on uninitialized stream state. The clone also silently lost the WindowLogMax limit. The flaw was… Used by Agave v4.4.1, Jito v4.4.1-jito: zstd-safe 8.0.0. Compiled into the release. Watch for a client release that updates this crate.

items.title: [WATCH] Out-of-bounds read with an out-of-range InBuffer::pos
items.content_text: InBuffer's fields are public, so safe code can set pos past the end of src. The position was passed to the C library unchecked, and ZSTD_seekable_compressStream, unlike the other streaming functions, does not validate it: it read past the end of the input slice, by up to the frame size, and compressed that memory into the output. The flaw was corrected by checking the position before every call into the C… Used by Agave v4.4.1, Jito v4.4.1-jito: zstd-safe 8.0.0. Compiled into the release. Watch for a client release that updates this crate.

items.title: [WATCH] Use-after-free when changing a multithreaded context with an unfinished frame
items.content_text: When a multithreaded frame (zstdmt feature, CParameter::NbWorkers) is left unfinished, its jobs may still be running on the worker threads: the C library only waits for them when the next frame starts, or when the context is freed. A session reset makes the context accept changes again in the meantime, so: - unloading the dictionary (load_dictionary, ref_cdict, ref_prefix, disable_dictionary, init*, or… Used by Agave v4.4.1, Jito v4.4.1-jito: zstd-safe 8.0.0. Compiled into the release. Watch for a client release that updates this crate.

items.title: [WATCH] WebAssembly allocator shim corrupts memory on allocation failure
items.content_text: On wasm32, zstd-sys provides malloc and free to the C library through a shim over Rust's allocator. The shim did not check for allocation failure: it wrote its size header to address 0 and returned address 4, which the C library used as a valid buffer. free(NULL) also read below address 0. Whenever the instance cannot grow its memory by what a frame asks for, a small crafted frame (a 9-byte header declaring a… Used by Agave v4.4.1, Jito v4.4.1-jito: zstd-sys 2.1.0+zstd.1.5.7. Compiled into the release. Watch for a client release that updates this crate.

items.content_text: A client kept the token from a Retry packet without any length limit and put it into the header of every Initial packet it sent afterwards. Initial datagrams are 1200 bytes. When the token and connection IDs left no room for the minimum payload, PacketBuilder::new computed a minimum packet size larger than the maximum, which only a debug assertion checked. On the next poll_transmit, debug builds panic, and… Used by Agave v4.4.1, Jito v4.4.1-jito: quinn-proto 0.11.18. Compiled into the release. Watch for a client release that updates this crate.

On these targets the receive loop set up its msghdr only once and looked at the MSG_TRUNC flag before checking whether recvmsg had failed. After a datagram larger than the receive… Used by Agave v4.4.1, Jito v4.4.1-jito: quinn-udp 0.5.5. Compiled into the release. Watch for a client release that updates this crate.

items.title: [CRITICAL] Linux Kernel Race Condition Vulnerability
items.content_text: Linux Kernel contains a race condition vulnerability which allows concurrent writes to the same AF_ALG socket causing data to be unpredictably interleaved and creating inconsistencies in the socket's internal state. Linux Kernel. Update or mitigate as the vendor advises. CISA lists this flaw as exploited in attacks (deadline 2026-09-21 for US agencies).

items.title: [CRITICAL] Linux Kernel Out-of-Bounds Write Vulnerability
items.content_text: Linux Kernel contains an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the ebtables SNAT target which allows an ARP sender hardware address rewrite to write directly into a nonlinear socket-buffer fragment backed by a splice-imported file page. The impacted product(s) could be end-of-life (EoL) and/or end-of-service (EoS). Users are advised to discontinue use and/or transition to a supported version. Linux Kernel. Update or mitigate as the vendor advises. CISA lists this flaw as exploited in attacks (deadline 2026-09-21 for US agencies).

items.title: [CRITICAL] Linux Kernel Improper Check for Unusual or Exceptional Conditions Vulnerability
items.content_text: Linux Kernel contains an improper check for unusual or exceptional conditions vulnerability in the TLS receive path which allows a zero-length record retrieved from the rx_list to bypass the intended recvmsg() record-type handling, potentially causing subsequent TLS records to be processed using incorrect zero-copy and queuing assumptions. The impacted product(s) could be end-of-life (EoL) and/or end-of-service… Linux Kernel. Update or mitigate as the vendor advises. CISA lists this flaw as exploited in attacks (deadline 2026-09-21 for US agencies).

items.title: [CRITICAL] Linux Kernel Unspecified Vulnerability
items.content_text: Linux Kernel contains an unspecified vulnerability that can allow for privilege escalation via IPv6 networking subsystem. This vulnerability can impact multiple products, including but not limited to Suse, Red Hat, and other products using Linux. Linux Kernel. Update or mitigate as the vendor advises. CISA lists this flaw as exploited in attacks (deadline 2026-08-30 for US agencies).

Linux Kernel. Update or mitigate as the vendor advises. CISA lists this flaw as exploited in attacks (deadline 2026-08-29 for US agencies).

items.title: [WATCH] Panic-safety unsoundness in Chunk, RingBuffer, and InlineArray (use-after-free / double-free)

If an element's Drop panics during the drop, the metadata update is skipped, so the container still treats the already-dropped elements as live. When the container's own Drop runs, those elements are visited again — a use-after-free / double-free reachable from safe Rust. The RingBuffer methods require the… Used by Agave v4.4.1, Jito v4.4.1-jito: sized-chunks 0.6.5. Compiled into the release. Watch for a client release that updates this crate.

items.title: [WATCH] event-listener allows !Send tags to cross thread boundaries via StackSlot
items.content_text: Affected versions of event-listener unconditionally implement Send and Sync for StackSlot , the stack-allocated listener type created by the listener! macro. This allows a !Send tag type set via Event::with_tag to be moved to another thread and accessed via StackSlot::wait, causing a data race in safe code. Used by Agave v4.4.1, Jito v4.4.1-jito: event-listener 5.3.1. Compiled into the release. Watch for a client release that updates this crate.

items.title: [WATCH] Potential use-after-free due to lack of panic safety in LruCache::pop()
items.content_text: LruCache::pop() in lru was not panic-safe. If the Drop implementation of a stored key panics during pop(), self.detach() is never called, leaving dangling pointers in the internal doubly-linked list. A subsequent cache operation that triggers eviction can then dereference these dangling pointers: - The node is freed from the map, but remains linked in the LRU list due to the skipped detach() call - When… Used by Agave v4.4.1, Jito v4.4.1-jito: lru 0.7.8. Compiled into the release. Watch for a client release that updates this crate.

items.title: [WATCH] ed25519-dalek Double Public Key Signing Function Oracle Attack

items.title: [INFO] Aliasing violation in OrdSet insertion
items.content_text: Inserting into an im::OrdSet (for example by collecting an iterator into one) can violate Rust's aliasing rules: Miri reports a stacked borrows violation in sized_chunks::Chunk::force_copy(), which is called during insertion, where a shared borrow is invalidated by a unique borrow before the read through it completes. This is undefined behavior, reachable from safe code. No fixed version is available, as the… Used by Agave v4.4.1, Jito v4.4.1-jito: im 15.1.0.
